reason: While the text differentiates between priests and non-priests, assigning them distinct roles and access levels to the sacred mountain (priests may approach after sanctification; the general people cannot approach), it does not assert that priest leaders are inherently superior to non-priest leaders. The passage emphasizes functional differentiation and hierarchical access (Moses → Aaron/priests → elders → people) rather than an explicit declaration of priest superiority. Furthermore, the text actually shows that even among priests, access is restricted—Aaron and the high priest do not go as far as Moses, and all priests are subject to the same prohibition against breaking through. The passage is descriptive of roles and restrictions, not prescriptive of superiority.
